reasoning: Group 1 (failure-driven) is kept in full and takes priority. Its seven edits are compact, each conditioned on a visible clue feature, and all of their targets match existing skill text. They are the singular-default replacement, the contestant-name-after-'right:' clarification, source ranking for archive lines, the anchor-echo gate, the brand-suffix extension, the plural geographic group rule, and the clean-the-string rule. From Group 2 (success-driven) I kept the four edits that cover patterns the failure patches do not touch. They are the procedural Rule 3 fallback, the slogan/code/bare-place bullets in Rule 1, the 'this team's <player>' bullet, and the head-noun extension with its explicit tie-breaker over the delete-clue-words test. The only change I made to Group 2 is that the 'this team's <player>' bullet now inserts after the 'One of these <role/title>' bullet. Both it and Group 1's anchor-echo gate were anchored on the same sentence, which would have made their order ambiguous. The two do not conflict, because 'this team's <player>' gives the team and the gate gives the owner or container. I checked for conflicts and found none. The singular default carves out names that are plural by nature, so it agrees with the plural geographic rule. The verbatim-archive override in Rule 3 is strengthened rather than weakened. No edit touches the protected slow-update block, and no per-task gold answers are embedded as new examples.

edits.target: - Use the singular form for a generic single object ('Well', not 'wells'), but keep the plural for crops, commodities and mass categories ('Bananas') or when the clue says 'these'/'ones'.
edits.content: - Default to the SINGULAR headword, even when the clue says 'these' or 'one of these' ('these nocturnal flying mammals' -> 'Bat', not 'bats'; 'Well', not 'wells'). Answer keys list the singular. Keep the plural only for crops, commodities and mass categories ('Bananas'), for names that are plural by nature (Great Lakes, Rockies), or when a verbatim archive answer (Rule 3) is printed in the plural.

edits.target: (the answer is the text between '|' and '. right:'/'wrong:')
edits.content: (the answer is the text between '|' and '. right:'/'wrong:'. The name AFTER 'right:' or 'wrong:' is a CONTESTANT who buzzed in, never the answer, even when it is the only name-like token: 'CLUE | Hamlet. right: Dave. Wrong: Sue' -> 'Hamlet')

edits.target: Before the answer tags, briefly quote the matched line.
edits.content: - SOURCE RANKING when passages disagree: (a) an archive or flashcard line ('Q: ... A: answer', 'CLUE | answer', ALL-CAPS 'CLUE, ANSWER') is final, even if a quoted contestant gave a wrong response in the same line; take what follows 'A:' or the comma. (b) News pages quoting the Q/A come next. (c) Forum or discussion-thread replies (Topix, Reddit, Yahoo Answers) that follow a posted clue are guesses and never beat (a). If any passage has (a), answer from it before using your own knowledge or a plausible-sounding synonym.

edits.target: Other named entities in the clue are anchors, never the answer.
edits.content: - ANCHOR-ECHO GATE (apply just before the answer tags): if your answer repeats a name, title or phrase already in the clue, it is almost certainly an anchor, not the answer. Resolve it by the clue's pattern: (a) "this state's / country's / city's / company's <product, team or landmark>" plus a named region, town or site -> the OWNER or CONTAINER (the country, state, city or company), never the named thing or place; (b) 'He/She' + a quoted song, album or book title, including a foreign-language or original-language title -> the PERSON who made it (novelist, composer, dramatist), never the title; (c) '<quoted phrase> this person, like <Name>' or 'such as <Name>' -> the ROLE or job the named person holds, in its plain form (with 'the' if the quoted phrase implies it), never the person's name. Exception: word-level clues ('the adverb in ...') may reuse a clue word.

Drop corporate suffixes and product-line words that follow a brand name when the clue asks for 'this company / brand / maker' ('McCormick', not 'McCormick & Company'; 'Mattel', not 'Mattel Toys'; 'Ford', not 'Ford Motor Company'). A trivia key lists the bare brand.

edits.target: - For titles, give the standard title without quotation marks and keep internal punctuation as written in the context ('M*A*S*H', not 'MASH film').
edits.content: - PLURAL GEOGRAPHIC GROUPS ('these mountains', 'these islands', 'this mountain range'): the clue already states the type word, so apply the delete-clue-words test and give the short plural name people use ('the Appalachians', 'the Andes'), not '<Name> Mountains' or '<Name> Islands'. The head-noun exception above does not apply to these.

edits.target: Brief reasoning belongs before the tags.
edits.content: - CLEAN THE STRING before tagging: passages are scraped, so a word may carry fused junk (stray capitals or letters, digits, markup, e.g. 'wordE', 'word2'). Never copy the junk. Take the clean form from another passage quoting the same text, or from your own knowledge of the quote. When the clue quotes a line and leaves off the last word ('... with salt and' this), the answer is the single next word of the real line and nothing more.

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content: - Otherwise, find the passage sentence that contains two or more of the clue's anchors (names, dates, place, verb) and read the missing entity off that sentence in the role the clue's verb or relation assigns. 'Named for her' / 'named in honor of' -> the honoree. 'X & Y captured this city' -> the object of the capture, not X or Y. Prefer the entity that recurs across several independent passages beside those anchors, and give its bare common name.

edits.target: answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content:
- A clue that is only a quoted slogan, motto, tagline, catchphrase or lyric asks for the person, team, company or product it was made for. Find the entity the passages pair with the exact phrase ('campaign slogan for X', 'known as the place with...') and give its standard name as the passages print it. Do not answer the slogan itself or a name already inside the quote.
- A bare code, abbreviation or symbol in the clue (airport code, state or country code, chemical symbol, ticker), including after a colon, asks for what it stands for. Use the passages that pair the code with a name and answer with the bare common name of the place, element or organization (e.g. 'LAX' -> 'Los Angeles'), never the code.
- A bare one- or two-word PLACE name as the whole clue, with passages that are only local pages, businesses or directories, asks for the larger region that contains it: the U.S. state for a U.S. town or neighborhood, the country for a foreign city. Give the level every passage repeats, not the clue word, the county or a census-style name.

edits.target: not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - 'this team's <player or coach>' asks for the team. Give its usual city-plus-nickname form as the passages print it and drop the league or sport word. This differs from 'this city's Sabres', where the clue already gives the nickname and the answer is the city alone.

The same holds when the clue's modifier is an unrelated word that names something else by itself (an animal or insect name on a dish): keep the head noun. In these cases the head-noun test beats the DELETE-CLUE-WORDS test.
